correctness.rationale: For a finite connected simple graph with n>=2, F²(x)-x=-L(f+g) and connectedness force f+g constant. A nonfixed 2-cycle has f+g≡1, so a cut S between first-round firing and waiting vertices has all c_v(S)>0. Solving the second firing inequalities gives independent intervals of exactly c_v(S) values, with lower total 2m-|S|; quotient complementary first-round colorings into one unordered cut gives the stated complete orbit generating polynomial. Every maximum cut has positive cross-degree at each vertex, giving minima 2m-q, maxima 2m+q-n and coefficient M(G); factor palindromicity gives P(z)=z^(4m-n)P(1/z). Standard MAX-CUT reduces to minimum-energy existence, and rooted-tree edge subset recursion is linear in arithmetic operations; the path two-state transfer matrix [[0,1],[1,2]] gives Pell. Independently enumerated all vertex-level states (0<=x_v<2deg(v)) for P3, K3, P4, C4 and K4, matching direct cut polynomials, extremes and reflection. Source reports a larger 72-graph verifier, but analytical proof—not saved logs—supports all graphs.

value.rationale: A complete energy-resolved dynamical orbit census across an arbitrary connected graph family is motivated by conserved mass and firing-period structure. It explains sharp existence and extreme multiplicity via canonical MaxCut, yields an NP-complete threshold decision, and affords efficient tree computation and a natural Pell path sequence. This is not only a textbook period bound or isolated finite integer computation.
